detaileddescription.para: Written when a map's ledger sequence is established (Ledger::setFull(), InboundLedger) while a nodestore reader thread reads it. Relaxed either way: it serves as a lookup hint for a nodestore keyed by hash.

briefdescription.para: The map's state.

detaileddescription.para: A getMissingNodes() walk writes it, through setInvalid() and clearSynching(), while whatever drives the acquisition reads it. The walk runs with the acquisition's lock released, so this is atomic rather than guarded.

briefdescription.para: Map is believed complete in database.

detaileddescription.para: Atomic because finishFetch() clears it on any nodestore reader thread, several of which can run at once.

briefdescription.para: Mark this map as "should be full": the local server wants every node it references in durable storage, so a nodestore miss is a gap to report.

detaileddescription.para: Publishes the ledger sequence before the flag. The sequence store is relaxed and the flag store is release, and finishFetch() reads the sequence only after acquiring the flag, so the one miss that withdraws the flag always reports the sequence stored here. Keeping both stores in one place is what makes that order impossible to get wrong.

parameterdescription.para: Sequence of the ledger this map belongs to, which the gap report names.

briefdescription.para: Add a known node at a specific position in the SHAMap during synchronization.

detaileddescription.para: This function is used when receiving nodes from peers during ledger synchronization. The node is inserted at the position specified by nodeID. The node must already have been deserialized.
A node that no valid tree can hold makes the map Invalid, which is terminal: the root hash committed to an impossible shape, so no peer can satisfy it.

A deserialized tree node to add.
Optional sync filter to track received nodes.

briefdescription.para: Record that the map is provably not the one it claims to be.

detaileddescription.para: Private because only the map itself can prove that, from a node that contradicts the hashes it is syncing against. Cannot fail, since Invalid outranks every other state; see trySetState().

briefdescription.para: Move the map to a new state, atomically.

detaileddescription.para: With clearSynching(), the only writer of state_ past construction, so the order between the states lives in one place: Invalid outranks all of them and is always stored, while every other transition is refused once the map is Invalid, which is what makes that verdict terminal. clearSynching() is narrower and moves only Synching.

parameterdescription.para: The state to move to.

simplesect.para: false if the map is Invalid and the requested state is not, leaving it unchanged; true otherwise.
